candidates.label: linear chain: inducer -> KinA -> RegB -> ProD
candidates.rationale: The module as designed and as the description narrates it: RegB is the only catalyst of the PreC conversion and nothing feeds back. This is the null against which the other two are scored — if the extra terms buy nothing, the information criteria should say so, and the honest answer is the simplest wiring. It is also the candidate the BX-11 conditions bear on most directly: with RegB activation blocked by more than 90%, this structure can only make ProD through the residual leak.

candidates.label: chain plus a direct KinA-catalysed conversion of PreC (coherent feedforward)
candidates.rationale: Adds one parameter to M1: KinA converts PreC directly, in parallel with RegB. This is the description's first open question stated as a model — whether anything besides RegB catalyses the conversion. It is separable from M1 by the BX-11 conditions specifically, because that is where the RegB route is off and the direct route is not, and the extra route is dose-graded through Aa rather than constant, which distinguishes it from a basal leak.

candidates.label: chain plus sequestration of active RegB by the product
candidates.rationale: Adds one parameter to M1: the product holds active RegB in an inactive complex BD, so RegB_p falls late where ProD is highest. prior_reactions describes the conversion only in a review (rx_7), below the variants' floor, so it is named in `missing` for the round's search.

decisions.decision: Three candidates as differences from the tested chain: the base, + the direct KinA route, + the sequestration of active RegB by the product.
decisions.rationale: The description leaves open whether a second route converts PreC and whether the product acts back on the module; each candidate adds one answer to the base.
decisions.alternatives_considered: both additions together (not needed to separate them)

evidence.supports: whether a RegB-independent route exists and whether the product acts back on the module
